clue.text: That male prisoner, losing face, is a little lower

indicators.note: a face is the front, so losing it means dropping the first letter of the word

blocks.note: the pronoun for a male person
a prisoner serving a life sentence

explanation.surface: A disgraced convict sinks a little lower in everyone's estimation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' is not 'more low' but 'one that lows', a cow; a little one is a HEIFER.
explanation.definitionFit: A heifer is a young cow, and a cow is something that moos, or lows, so it is a small lower.

clue.text: What holds collar up for a long time

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is read from bottom to top
one word holding another keeps it inside its own letters

blocks.note: 'What?' and 'Eh?' are both ways of asking someone to repeat themselves
to collar or cop someone is to arrest them

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about something that keeps a shirt collar raised for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collar' looks like a shirt part but is the verb to arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is an era, a long period of history.

clue.text: Some relief I'd get, in grumpy thumb twiddling?

indicators.note: some of the following words means only part of their run of letters is used

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of relief to the start of grumpy

explanation.surface: A bored, grumpy person hopes twiddling their thumbs will bring some relief.
explanation.definitionFit: Twiddling one's thumbs is a restless, idle movement, which is a kind of fidgeting.

clue.text: Tramp with working alternative to spray can

blocks.note: to roll is to wander about, as a tramp does
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A vagrant carries a working replacement for an aerosol can.
explanation.walkthrough: The spray can is a deodorant aerosol; the other common form is applied with a rolling ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll-on is a deodorant dispensed by a ball applicator, the usual alternative to an aerosol.

clue.text: Cerebrally satirical pop star – Blockheads front man?

blocks.note: Taylor Swift, the pop star
Ian Dury fronted the band Ian Dury and the Blockheads

explanation.surface: Musing on whether a clever, satirical pop star could front the Blockheads.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian Dury and the Blockheads were a British new wave band of the late 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: Jonathan Swift wrote biting, intellectual satire such as Gulliver's Travels, so writing in his manner is Swiftian.

clue.text: Old school mercenary odds-on to need retraining

indicators.note: something needing retraining must be taught again and reshaped into a new form

blocks.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: A soldier of fortune is near-certain to need retraining for civilian life.
explanation.walkthrough: A secondary modern was a British state school for pupils who did not get into a grammar school, largely phased out from the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: Secondary moderns are a largely abolished type of British school, so it is an old school in both senses.

clue.text: Precarious, easy job after moving home

indicators.note: moving a part means taking it from where it stood and putting it elsewhere, here at the front

blocks.note: someone at home is in
a sinecure is a paid post with little work

explanation.surface: A cushy job turns out to be shaky once the worker relocates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving home' reads like relocating house; here the letters for home shift from the middle of the word to its front.
explanation.definitionFit: Something precarious is unstable and not firmly fixed, which is what insecure means.

clue.text: Cycling around, criticise e-vehicle

indicators.note: cycling letters round moves some from one end of the word to the other, keeping their order

blocks.note: to slate is to criticise harshly

explanation.surface: A cyclist going round criticises electric cars.
explanation.walkthrough: The last two letters of SLATE come round to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Tesla is the best-known maker of electric cars, so a Tesla is an e-vehicle.

clue.text: News broadcaster – American news broadcaster ultimately carrying weight

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word before it
carrying something means holding it within, so one piece goes inside the others

blocks.note: A is short for American, and N is short for new, so 'news' read as a plural gives two of them
the last letter of broadcaster
an ounce is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: An American newsreader carries some weight with the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the opening 'News broadcaster'; the second 'news' is wordplay, read as more than one 'new'.
explanation.definitionFit: An announcer is a presenter who reads out the news or introduces programmes on radio or TV.

clue.text: Fabled housebreaker, mature one, breaking good protective devices

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
mature means grown old
I is the Roman numeral one
locks protect doors

explanation.surface: An older burglar from a fable breaks through good security locks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Housebreaker' suggests a real burglar, but the fable is the story of the three bears.
explanation.definitionFit: In the fairy tale Goldilocks enters the three bears' house uninvited, so she is a housebreaker from a story.

clue.text: Tory leader with no answer getting dropped

indicators.note: with no means that one thing is left out of the word

blocks.note: Rishi Sunak led the Conservative (Tory) Party
A is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: A Conservative leader with no answers gets dumped by his party.
explanation.walkthrough: Rishi Sunak was Conservative Party leader and UK Prime Minister 2022 to 2024.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunk is a past participle of sink, so it means dropped down or gone under.

clue.text: Leaving university, he honours organised help for getting into Oxford?

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so it is taken out of the letters
organised means arranged, so these letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: U is the abbreviation for university
taken as written

explanation.surface: A graduate leaving university arranges honours to help someone get into Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford is not the university but a laced leather shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoehorn is a curved tool that helps the heel slip into a shoe such as an Oxford brogue.

clue.text: Boater, say, getting into vessel for romance

indicators.note: getting into something means going inside it

blocks.note: a boater is a flat straw hat
a cup is a drinking vessel

explanation.surface: A rower boarding a boat in search of a romantic encounter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boater' and 'vessel' suggest rowing, but the boater is a straw hat and the vessel holds drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: To romance someone is to woo them, and to chat up is to talk flirtatiously to someone you fancy.

clue.text: You heard pound gets pocketed by American who serves fruit

indicators.note: heard means we use how the word sounds, not how it is spelt
being pocketed means being put inside something else

blocks.note: the letter U sounds like the word you
a GI is an American soldier
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: You hear that a pound coin was pocketed by an American fruit seller.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside GI, after U. 'Who serves' tells us the American is a serviceman.
explanation.definitionFit: An ugli is a Jamaican citrus fruit, a cross between a grapefruit and a tangerine.

clue.text: Ecstasy over record, in essence, for a rock enthusiast

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the next word

blocks.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over
a log is a record, as in a ship's log
the gist is the essence of something

explanation.surface: Ecstasy and a record seem to be the essence of being a rock music fan.
explanation.walkthrough: The rock fan here likes stones, not music; the first three pieces sit inside the essence word just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A geologist studies rocks scientifically, so is literally a rock enthusiast.

clue.text: Sky broadcast, special one

blocks.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
SP is an abbreviation for special
an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: A one-off special broadcast on Sky television.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky is the British satellite TV network, which makes 'broadcast' look like part of a TV story.
explanation.definitionFit: Airspace is the region of sky above a territory, so sky stands in for it.

clue.text: City coach and Escort boarded by northern clerk

indicators.note: a thing boarded by something has that something come aboard, inside it

blocks.note: Pep Guardiola is manager of Manchester City football club
N is the abbreviation for northern
an usher escorts people to their seats

explanation.surface: A northern clerk climbs aboard a city coach with an escort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' looks like a bus and 'Escort' like a Ford car, but they are a football manager and an usher.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen-pusher is a disparaging term for a clerk or office worker doing routine paperwork.

clue.text: It creates romantic illusions in squiffy arts students? Not half!

indicators.note: not half means half of the word is dropped
squiffy means tipsy, so the letters lurch into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
half of it is kept

explanation.surface: Tipsy arts students fall for romantic illusions, and how!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'very much so', but here it drops the second half of students.
explanation.definitionFit: Stardust is a dreamy, romantic quality said to cast an enchanting spell on people.

clue.text: Like some car parks in pines beside Scottish river

blocks.note: to pine for something is to long for it
the Tay is Scotland's longest river

explanation.surface: Car parks set among pine trees beside a river in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pines' looks like trees but is the verb meaning yearns.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-stay car parks, at airports for example, are designed for vehicles left for days.

clue.text: Model student at Hogwarts going over tip for magic

indicators.note: going over means turning back on itself, so the name is read right to left
the tip of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: Ron Weasley studies at Hogwarts in Harry Potter
the first letter of magic

explanation.surface: A model pupil at the wizarding school goes over a magic tip.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm is a standard or pattern to follow, which is one sense of model.

clue.text: The deep crimson perhaps turned black

blocks.note: the deep is a poetic name for the sea
crimson is a shade of red

explanation.surface: A deep crimson colour that has darkened to black.
explanation.definitionFit: Searing scorches a surface until it browns or blackens, so seared means burned dark.

clue.text: More in jail

blocks.note: first meaning: more fashionable, as 'in' means trendy
second meaning: slang for prison

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as 'more people in jail'; in fact 'in' is the adjective trendy and the comparative is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooler is the comparative of cool, meaning trendy, and also slang for a prison cell.

clue.text: Both sides shielding ball around Spanish playmaker

indicators.note: shielding something means surrounding it to protect it

blocks.note: L and R stand for left and right
a ball is round like the letter O
ca is short for circa, meaning around

explanation.surface: Defenders on both flanks shield the ball around a Spanish midfielder.
explanation.walkthrough: The playmaker is not a footballer but a maker of plays: Federico García Lorca.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorca was a Spanish dramatist, author of Blood Wedding, so he made plays.

clue.text: Tired from a series of deliveries, resorted to drugs?

blocks.note: in cricket an over is a series of six balls
to use is slang for taking drugs

explanation.surface: A bowler, exhausted after an over, turned to drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: A tired phrase is a hackneyed one, worn out from being used too often.

clue.text: Partner of Eric Clapton's back, dunked in lake

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter
something dunked in is plunged inside

blocks.note: Lake Erie, one of the Great Lakes
the last letter of Clapton

explanation.surface: Eric Clapton's partner dunked his back in a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eric' looks like Clapton, but the partner is from the British comedy double act Morecambe and Wise, Eric and Ernie.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernie Wise was the comic partner of Eric Morecambe for over forty years.

clue.text: Free dresses zip the wrong way for designer

indicators.note: dressing something means wrapping it, so it goes inside
the wrong way means read backwards

blocks.note: to rid is to free
zip is slang for nothing, zero

explanation.surface: Free dresses whose zips are put in back to front by a designer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dresses' looks like clothing but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Christian Dior was a French fashion designer whose house still bears his name.

clue.text: Finding upper-class event which almost goes wrong

blocks.note: U is the abbreviation for upper-class
a near thing is a narrow escape

explanation.surface: A posh party that very nearly turns into a disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Unearthing something means discovering it after a search, as in digging it up.

clue.text: Reportedly get the Kinks out of distress

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is spoken, so the sound counts and not the spelling

blocks.note: to remove kinks is to make straight

explanation.surface: Getting the band the Kinks out of trouble, so it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: The Kinks were a 1960s British rock band, but here kinks are bends.
explanation.definitionFit: To straiten is to put into difficulty or hardship, as in straitened circumstances, which is to distress.

clue.text: Cursed what needleworker did

blocks.note: first meaning: a mild euphemism for damned
second meaning: mended holes with needle and thread

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a sewer swearing; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Darned is a polite stand-in for damned, and also the past tense of darn, to repair by stitching.
